For each flagged item, rule whether the key's answer is uniquely defensible from the evidence (key-uniquely-defensible), whether two answers are defensible (ambiguous), or whether the key is wrong (key-wrong). 3	Answer semantics:
4	- hypothesis: "supported" = the evidence, taken together, supports the claim more than its rivals; "contradicted" = the evidence counts against it; "unknown" = the evidence does not discriminate, so the claim is live but unestablished.
5	- edge (a claimed link from one condition to another): "causal" = the evidence supports a causal link (for example temporal order plus mechanism plus covariation with the main rival ruled out, a natural experiment, or an intervention result); "association-only" = they co-occur or correlate in the evidence but causation is not established; "contradicted" = evidence counts against the link; "unknown" = evidence is insufficient even to show association.
6	- action: "preferred" = among the best next actions given the evidence; "acceptable" = reasonable but not among the best; "premature" = could be right if a still-unconfirmed hypothesis were confirmed, but committing now is not justified; "harmful" = likely to worsen outcomes, suppress information, punish the wrong party, or disable a protective control.
7	- sufficiency (item SUFF): is the evidence sufficient to commit to the action you rank highest, where that action is substantive rather than merely evidence-gathering? "sufficient" or "insufficient". Concluding that no intervention is warranted counts as a substantive decision.
8	- Items with asOfStage set must be answered using only evidence whose stage is at or before that stage.

10	Truth convention: expected answers are what a careful analyst concludes after reading the initial file plus the optimal read path (at most three catalogue items); for INCOMPLETE and NOCONC cases, what the whole catalogue supports.

338	CASE OD2-HO-NOCONC-1 (NOCONC, organizational): Two quarters of rising shrink at a mid-size variety store
339	Setting: Marrowby Stores is a fictional regional grocery and general-merchandise chain with 38 stores. Its fiscal year matches the calendar year (Q1 = January–March). Store 14 in Dunmere is a mid-size store with about $2.8 million in quarterly sales. Quarterly shrink figures go to regional leadership. Asset Protection has been asked to review store 14. Today is 10 November FY2026.
340	Presenting request: Regional Director Imelda Charroux wants a plan for store 14 by month-end. Regional Operations needs a decision on the December count by 20 November. Work out what explains the store's rising shrink and recommend what to do next.
341	INITIAL EVIDENCE
342	E1 [stage S1] Email from Imelda Charroux, Regional Director (North), 2 Nov (leadership-account): To: Asset Protection. Re: Store 14, Dunmere. Store 14's shrink has climbed two quarters running: 1.5% of sales in Q1, 1.9% in Q2 and 2.3% in Q3, against a chain average of 1.6% in each quarter. That is roughly $24,000 more loss in Q3 than in Q1. Two consecutive rises is a trend, not noise. The four self-checkout lanes went live on 17 March, right before this started, and the vendor's Q3 report shows 412 unscanned-item interventions at the store. Every trade article I read says self-checkout drives shrink. I want a plan by month-end to either pull the lanes or staff them full-time.
343	E2 [stage S1] Interview notes, store manager Dorian Pask, 3 Nov (manager-account): Pask does not think self-checkout is the issue. He believes shoplifting has grown since the Dunmere bus interchange opened beside the car park on 16 February. Door-counter footfall averaged 14,100 visits a week in Q1, 15,200 in Q2 and 15,900 in Q3. He cites recorded shoplifting incidents in the store log: 6 in Q1, 11 in Q2 and 15 in Q3, mostly razors, cosmetics and batteries. 'My team is logging more than they ever have. We need a guard on the door.' Asked whether staff theft could be involved, he said he trusts his team and pointed to the ethics-line case being closed.
344	E3 [stage S1] Ethics-line case 26-0871 and asset protection follow-up (log): Received 21 Aug, anonymous caller: 'The night stocker at Dunmere [name redacted] keeps taking boxes out the back door after close. Saw it on the 12th and the 19th.' Follow-up by AP investigator R. Okafor, 2 Sep: Reviewed rear-door and dock CCTV for 12 and 19 August, 22:00–06:00. On both nights the named stocker made two trips through the rear door carrying flattened cardboard bales to the compactor, as listed on the closing checklist. No merchandise or sealed cartons seen leaving. Night supervisor confirms bale runs are assigned to this employee. Case closed: unsubstantiated.
345	E4 [stage S1] Store 14 interim shrink report, Q1–Q3 FY2026 (financial-record): Shrink as % of department sales, Q1 / Q2 / Q3. Grocery 0.8 / 1.1 / 1.3. Fresh 1.6 / 2.0 / 2.4. Health & beauty 2.9 / 3.6 / 4.4. General merchandise 2.0 / 2.5 / 3.1. Store total 1.5 / 1.9 / 2.3. Each department's share of store sales stayed within one point across all three quarters: grocery 46%, fresh 24%, health & beauty 14%, general merchandise 16%. Footnote: Q1–Q3 figures are interim estimates extrapolated from rotating department cycle counts. The annual full physical count, carried out by the independent count contractor, is scheduled for 7 December.
346	E5 [stage S1] Email from Bram Castellane, Regional Operations Manager, 6 Nov (manager-account): Re: December count, store 14. Given holiday staffing pressure, I propose we take store 14 out of the 7 December full physical count and roll forward the Q3 book figure for year-end. We already know where that store's number is heading, and the count costs about 140 staff hours plus contractor fees. The other 37 stores would count as planned. Please confirm by 20 November so the contractor can re-plan its schedule.

348	C1 [stage S1] Store 14 staff roster and turnover summary, January–September FY2026 - HR information system extract (system-record): HR extract, store 14, Jan–Sep FY2026. Headcount ranged from 58 to 61. Leavers 9, starters 11 (annualised turnover 31%; chain median 34%). Night replenishment crew: five staff, unchanged since October FY2025 apart from one replacement on 11 May. The assistant store manager changed on 7 July (internal transfer). No disciplinary cases were opened at the store in the period. Two staff were on long-term leave during Q2.
349	C2 [stage S1] Self-checkout vendor briefing on shrink outcomes at client retailers - Slide notes from the self-checkout vendor's account manager, 30 Oct (vendor-account): 'Across our retail clients, stores in their first year of self-checkout typically see shrink 0.3–0.5 points higher than before installation, falling back as attendants gain experience. Our VisionAssist camera upgrade cuts unscanned-item loss by up to 40% and can be installed at Dunmere within three weeks for all four lanes. We recommend Marrowby prioritise store 14 given its Q3 shrink figure.' No client names or underlying data were provided with the slides.
350	C3 [stage S1] Interim shrink by SKU class, store 14, Q3 versus Q1 FY2026 - Finance inventory analytics extract (financial-record): The $23,800 increase in interim shrink dollars between Q1 and Q3 is spread across 61 of 74 SKU classes. Largest contributors: razor blades $1,900, cosmetics $1,600, batteries $1,100, pet food $1,000, canned fish $900, small kitchenware $800. The top ten classes account for 41% of the increase. Fresh produce and bakery together account for 14%. Analyst note: per-class interim figures carry wider error than the store total and should not be read in isolation.
351	C4 [stage S1] Police calls for service coded retail theft, Dunmere district, Q4 FY2025–Q3 FY2026 - Dunmere police district open-data portal (external-data): Calls for service coded 'retail theft', all premises in the district: Q4 FY2025 43, Q1 FY2026 41, Q2 47, Q3 44. Of these, calls from Marrowby store 14: 2, 1, 3, 2. The district covers 23 retail premises. A note on the portal says most low-value shoplifting is not reported to police by retailers, so call counts are a partial measure of retail theft.

Tickets 4471, 4502 and 4590: replacement terminals back-ordered. 26 Jun: replacement terminals installed and certified; lanes back in service on 27 Jun. Vendor monthly summary, Q3: self-checkout handled 18% of store 14 transactions; 412 unscanned-item interventions, or 28.6 per 1,000 self-checkout transactions. Median across the 12 Marrowby stores with self-checkout: 30.4 (range 21–41).

rulings.explanation: The SUFF definition asks whether the evidence is sufficient to commit to the top-ranked action 'where that action is substantive rather than merely evidence-gathering'. Reading the question as 'is the evidence sufficient to do A1?' ignores the 'substantive rather than merely evidence-gathering' clause in the definition.
